CORS|Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: A security feature implemented in web browsers and configured by the contacted server in the response's header to the AJAX requests made via the browser (L5 slide 18). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
Same-Origin Policy|SOP: The default browser policy that the HTML files containing the AJAX requests are hosted in the same origin as the server-side scripts answering them (L5 slide 18). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
origin: The combination of domain, protocol and port; 80 is the default for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS (L5 slide 18). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
preflight request|preflight: An OPTIONS request the browser sends first to check whether the server permits the intended cross-origin request (L5 slide 20; Quiz 10). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: The response header that tells the browser what origins can send requests to this server; "*" means everyone (L5 slide 19). See [Coding questions: Node servers, XHR, promise chains, CORS and query strings](#/comp4537-midterm/coding-questions).
idempotent|idempotency: Can be applied multiple times without changing the result; PUT is idempotent, POST is not (L6 slide 3). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
readyState: The status of the XMLHttpRequest: 0 UNSENT, 1 OPENED, 2 HEADERS_RECEIVED, 3 LOADING, 4 DONE (L5 slide 8, L6 slide 55). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
XMLHttpRequest|XHR: The object a page creates to send an AJAX request, "just like the way we created Date object" (L5 slide 7). See [Coding questions: Node servers, XHR, promise chains, CORS and query strings](#/comp4537-midterm/coding-questions).
status code|status: The http response type your server script returns: 200 OK, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error, 5xx server error (L5 slide 8). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
event queue|callback queue: Where a timer's callback waits until the call stack is empty, which is why the script prints 1, 3, 2 even with 0 ms (L1 slide 162). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
microtask|microtask queue: Where promise handlers are put; they run only after the current call stack finishes (L6 slide 17). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
call stack|current call stack: The synchronous code running now; promise handlers wait only for the current call stack to unwind (L6 slide 17). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
hoisting: The engine treats var declarations as if they were declared at the top of the function or script, so reading one early prints undefined (L1 slide 132). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
function scope|function-scoped: A var is accessible in the entire function it was declared in (L1 slides 115, 127). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
block scope|block-scoped: A let or const is accessible only within the block, the lines of code within {}, it was declared in (L1 slides 115, 127). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
falsy: Undefined, null, 0, false, NaN and '' (empty string) all mean false in the condition part of an if statement (L1 slide 114).
primitive|primitive data type: One of the six ES6 types Boolean, null, undefined, Number, String, Symbol; everything else is an object (L1 slide 113).
promise|Promise: An object used for asynchronous computations, representing a single asynchronous operation that hasn't completed yet (L6 slide 16). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
executor|executer: The function passed to the Promise constructor; it gets executed immediately upon creation of the promise object (L6 slide 17). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
pending: The promise state before it is fulfilled or rejected: you don't know yet (L6 slide 13).
fulfilled|resolved: The promise state after resolve() has run; older Chrome showed it as "resolved" (L6 slides 13, 37).
rejected: The promise state after reject() has run (L6 slide 13).
settled: Fulfilled or rejected; once settled, the state will not change (L6 slides 14, 24).
async function|async: A function declared async automatically returns a promise (L6 slide 52). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
await: Used inside async functions to wait for a promise to resolve or reject (L6 slide 52). See [What prints: twenty programs on timers, scope, hoisting and promises](#/comp4537-midterm/output-order-drill).
callback: A function passed to another function, "the function to call once you are done" (L6 slide 5). See [Coding questions: Node servers, XHR, promise chains, CORS and query strings](#/comp4537-midterm/coding-questions).
callback hell: Nesting each next asynchronous call inside the previous one's callback to guarantee order (L6 slide 40). See [Coding questions: Node servers, XHR, promise chains, CORS and query strings](#/comp4537-midterm/coding-questions).
REST|RESTful: Representational State Transfer, an architectural style or set of constraints for API communication, not an architectural pattern (L3 slides 45, 48). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
stateless: Each request contains all the info needed; the server doesn't store session state (L3 slide 50). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
uniform interface: REST's core constraint: resources identified by URIs, nouns in the URL, verbs as HTTP methods (L3 slide 51). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
API gateway|gateway: The single entry point every request goes through; responsible for routing, authentication, auditing (L3 slide 47). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
endpoint: The URL where the API server is listening (L3 slide 32). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
query string: Name/value pairs sent in the URL of a GET request, after the ? (L3 slide 34). See [Coding questions: Node servers, XHR, promise chains, CORS and query strings](#/comp4537-midterm/coding-questions).
monolithic architecture|monolith: All application logic bundled together in one deployable unit (L2 slide 11). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
microservices|microservice architecture: A collection of loosely coupled, independently deployable services (L2 slide 20). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
non-blocking: Node sends a task and is ready for the next request before the file is read, like one waiter serving every table (L4 slides 12, 18). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
serialize|JSON.stringify: Turning an object into a JSON string so it can be sent or stored; JSON.parse deserializes it back (L2 slide 28). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
localStorage: Web storage with no expiration date, per origin (L2 slide 33). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
sessionStorage: Web storage for one session; data is lost when the browser tab is closed (L2 slide 33). See [Short and medium answers: the definitions and comparisons the exam asks for](#/comp4537-midterm/short-answer-drill).
CRUD: Create, Read, Update, Delete (L5 slide 32, L2 slide 24).
